summary: Angeles NF peak lookout; planned 1922, built 1927-35 per one source (register says 1935); cab moved to Vetter Mountain and burned 2009; footings reported.

facts.design: Region 5 Plan 4A cabin on a 10-foot X-brace open steel tower; may later have been replaced by a BC-301 design
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Angeles National Forest
facts.status_note: The cab was moved to Vetter Mountain in 1937 and burned there in 2009; a rebuilt lookout now stands on Vetter Mountain. Concrete footings are reported, but the sources do not say clearly whether they are on the summit or at Vetter Mountain.

events.note: Trail being built to the summit and a fire lookout contemplated, per a 1922 Los Angeles Times item; a plan, not a build date
Angeles Adventures: a lookout tower built in 1927 or 1928; the site is dated 1927-1935
Register 'Built' field; the register's description also says the cabin was constructed as early as 1922; conflicts with the 1927-28 build date
Observer for the previous season, per a February 1930 Monrovia News-Post report; Angeles Adventures names Glenn Moore as a lookout in 1929 instead
Covina Argus, May 1934: lookouts stationed on San Gabriel Peak that Saturday
Cab dismantled in 1937 and moved to Vetter Mountain, per Angeles Adventures
The structure at Vetter Mountain burned in the 2009 Station Fire, per Angeles Adventures; the Vetter Mountain lookout's original tower was destroyed in August 2009, per ANFFLA
Vetter Mountain lookout rebuilt with Southern California Edison, construction began 2019 and was completed April 2020 (ANFFLA); the sources do not say whether it reuses the San Gabriel cab

notes_for_editor: Build date is disputed: the register's Built field says 1935 but its description says the cabin was constructed as early as 1922; the 1922 LA Times item was a plan, and Angeles Adventures says 1927-28 with operation to 1935. The 1937 move to Vetter Mountain rests on Angeles Adventures quoting D. Von Schmausen's Vetter Mountain paper, which we did not read. The 2009 loss and 2019-2020 rebuild come from ANFFLA and match the existing us-ca-vetter-mountain record, which also notes a 1935 vs 1937 build-year conflict; both records point to the same lookout but do not show it is the San Gabriel cab. The footings line in Angeles Adventures may refer to Vetter Mountain rather than the summit, so today's remains on San Gabriel Peak are unconfirmed. Both Vetter cabs are 14 by 14 feet, which fits the move but is not proof. Staffing names disagree (Mathys for the 1929 season in the 1930 paper; Glenn Moore in 1929 per Angeles Adventures). No access rule was found for the summit, so no access key is set. Worth a look: whether the 1937 relocation belongs in the Vetter Mountain record.
